function: Learned precoder (PMI) and rank (RI) selection for coordinated BSs via hierarchical RL, with a diffusion-generated representative channel to fix PMI, RI, CQI per location (pp. 1, 6-9)
system: Two coordinated downlink BSs with 16 Tx antennas each (8x1 dual-polarized UPA), UE with 4 Rx antennas, MIMO-OFDM 72 subcarriers, 3.5 GHz, no RIS (p. 10, Table I)
method: Hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning with transformer-encoder Q-network (replay buffer, epsilon-greedy) for PMI and RI; generative training of a conditional diffusion model (U-Net) for channel generation (pp. 6-9)
data_channel: 3GPP 38.901 CDL (p. 3) on DeepMIMO Outdoor 1 ray-tracing scenario at 3.5 GHz, 1138 UE positions, 100 time-varied subframes, simulated in the Vienna 5G link-level simulator (p. 10)
test_conditions: Trained and evaluated on the same 2-BS Outdoor 1 scenario, 3.5 GHz, 1138 positions and 100 subframes; no unseen scenario, band, antenna setup or held-out positions (pp. 7, 10-12)
baselines: Non-learned: 1-DBS CLSM, 2-DBS heuristic codebook iteration (HCI), 1st-subframe parameters. Learned: conditional VAE [19], averaged-reward T-HRL, HRL without transformer, 4 networks, 1 network (pp. 10-12)
metrics: UE throughput (Mbit/s), mutual information (training reward), BER, CDF of throughput and BER (pp. 10-12)
q1_support: p. 3: "we use the clustered delay line (CDL) defined in 3GPP 38.901 [38] to model the channel impulse response (CIR)"; p. 10: "We use the Outdoor 1 scenario provided by DeepMIMO [46]".
q2_support: p. 10: "We consider a simulation setting consisting of 2 DBS and 1138 UE positions"; results are shown at those same 1138 locations (p. 11, Fig. 9) with one scenario, band and antenna setup. Missing: any unseen scenario, band, antenna setup, held-out positions or adaptation. Fig. 14 (p. 12) only sweeps the number of subframes used to generate the channel.
q3_support: p. 11: "achieves up to 97% UE throughput of the HCI method and significantly enhances the performance of the CLSM transmission" (non-learned, throughput); p. 12: "we compare the feedback-free transmission performance with an averaged reward method and a conditional VAE approach in [19]" (earlier learned VAE method for the same function, p. 3, throughput in Fig. 14).
q4_support: Not met. p. 7: "avoiding the exponential dimensionality" ... "for the action space of D DBSs" is the action-space size of a centralized alternative, and p. 11 only calls HCI "linear complexity" and CLSM "exponential complexity"; no order, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime of the proposed HRL or diffusion model is reported.
q5_support: p. 10: "We use the Outdoor 1 scenario provided by DeepMIMO [46]" and Fig. 4 caption "DeepMIMO 3.5 GHz 3D ray-tracing scenario"; no link to the authors' own code or data is given.
notes: Area 3: the learned HRL selects PMI and RI (base station precoder and rank) and the main metric is UE throughput (pp. 1, 6-7); the diffusion model only synthesizes a representative channel used to fix PMI, RI and CQI (p. 8), and CQI comes from an EESM lookup table (p. 6). q1 is met by 3GPP 38.901 CDL (p. 3) and the DeepMIMO scenario (p. 10). q5 rests only on the public DeepMIMO Outdoor 1 scenario (p. 10): the time-varying channels are generated with CDL in MATLAB on top of it (p. 10), so the reviewer should confirm. q4 is 0 because the p. 7 O() remark concerns the action space avoided, not the cost of the method.
